# lean-pkg publish

the checklist from verified-private to listed, with the exact next commands (read-only); --yes makes the repository public (`promote` is the same).

Also spelled: `lean-pkg promote` ([all aliases](aliases.md)).

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg publish [--yes] [--dry-run] [--public-safety] [--corroborate] [--attested]
                 [--trusted-root FILE] [--skip-public-safety] [--agent AGENT]
                 [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--yes` | publish: run the promotion checklist, then gh repo edit --visibility public (ONE-WAY); first fetches origin's branches, tags and pull-request heads so the public-safety scan covers them (a failed fetch refuses). With --dry-run: the same checklist, nothing flipped |
| `--dry-run` | write nothing (the default without --yes); with --yes: the promotion checklist only |
| `--public-safety` | read-only checklist: also scan the tree and git history for private patterns (`lean-pkg public-safety`); --yes always scans |
| `--corroborate` | read-only checklist: render the page line as `page --check --corroborate` does, asking the public GitHub REST API about each GitHub Actions job (level 2), so a README carrying the GitHub Actions sentence can pass; GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN only raises the rate limit |
| `--attested` | read-only checklist: render the page line as `page --check --attested` does, verifying each GitHub Actions job's committed Sigstore bundle with `gh attestation verify` (level 3), which holds after the run has expired from the API; with --corroborate too, level 2 must also hold, so after expiry drop --corroborate |
| `--trusted-root FILE` | with --attested: verify offline against this Sigstore trusted root (gh attestation verify --custom-trusted-root) |
| `--skip-public-safety` | with --yes: do not run the public-safety scan of the tree and history (a WARN line instead; the scan covers the whole repository when the package is a subdirectory of it) |
| `--agent AGENT` | with --yes: the agent acting (recorded as the promoted event's actor); another agent's live lease then refuses |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `publish NAME` | read-only release checklist from verified-private to listed (`--dry-run` says so explicitly and changes nothing): the `page --check` line (a WARN while the package has no `coverage.yaml` and no page block, a failure for an unbacked Easley sentence; JSON `page`; with `--corroborate`, rendered as `page --check --corroborate` renders it, so a README carrying the GitHub Actions sentence can pass, the checklist's only network use; not with `--yes`; with `--attested [--trusted-root FILE]`, rendered as `page --check --attested` renders it: each job's committed Sigstore bundle is verified with `gh attestation verify` (level 3), which still holds after the run has expired from the GitHub API and `--corroborate` can no longer succeed, so after expiry check with `--attested` instead of `--corroborate` (under both flags level 3 needs both answers; a failed bundle with a corroborated run is level 2 with a warning); `--json` `page` then gains `sites` {name: {level, levels}} and `warnings[]` (also on stderr); not with `--yes`, and `--trusted-root` needs `--attested` and an existing file, exit 2); the promotion checklist of `--yes`, claims ledger included (for a `verified-private` package; `--json` `claims_ledger` as with `--yes`, null otherwise; a public one only needs HEAD pushed), consent recorded, `license_spdx` set and the LICENSE text matching it, `formalization.yaml` present, schema-valid and equal to the render (stale evidence is a `✗`; missing is a `✗` for `upstream_target: palomar`, else `WARN`), `claims.yaml` synced at HEAD when tracked, a Lake package name in the lakefile, a tag at HEAD (`WARN`); then the exact next commands (`publish NAME --yes --dry-run`, `publish NAME --yes`, `git tag`/push, `record reservoir-listed`, `record palomar-submitted`; the tag push names the checkout's GitHub remote, found by URL among `git remote -v` since `origin` may be a private mirror, says "after publish --yes" while the package is not public, and says so when no remote points at GitHub). The git-ignored evidence `WARN` of `--yes` (for any status) and `--json` `ignored_evidence[]` {path, rule}. Exit 0 when no `✗`, else 1; `--json`: `ready`, `checklist[]`, `next[]`, `manuscript_findings` (the ledger's summary of what the formalization found in the manuscript, also one text line `manuscript findings (what the formalization found): ...` when there is one; never a checklist item, never a status; [Lifecycle](../lifecycle.md#manuscript-findings)). `--public-safety` adds the `public-safety` scan as a checklist line (the `--yes` refusal text when it has hits; `--json` gains `public_safety`); a `WARN` item `palomar: not submittable ...` when `palomar check` finds error gaps at HEAD (JSON `palomar_check`, as in `gate --check`), and, while the docs-only opt-in exists only in the registry record (`docs_descendants: true`, no `lean-pkg-binding.yaml` at the gate-bound commit), a `WARN` item, a stderr `WARN: deprecated: ...` line and JSON `deprecations[]` naming `update NAME --write-binding-file` ([docs-only descendants](../receipts.md#docs-only-descendants-opt-in)); it never makes the checklist fail | `[--dry-run]` `[--public-safety]` `[--corroborate]` `[--attested [--trusted-root FILE]]` |
| `publish NAME --yes` | publish: the promotion checklist, then the GitHub repository goes public (one-way); `--yes --dry-run` runs the checklist and flips nothing (the pre-1.0 `publish NAME --yes --dry-run`; `publish NAME --yes` is `publish NAME --yes`). The checklist requires the claims ledger at the promote stage to be `ready` (every `reusable` claim verified, theorems and lemmas by the comparator tier too; a package without claims is `unknown` and refused; the line is `claims ledger ready: N required claim(s) verified (sha256:…)` or `claims ledger STATUS: REASON; first: ID: CODE` naming `claims ledger NAME`; `--json` gains `claims_ledger` {package_status, counts, required, reasons, ledger_digest}; see [Lifecycle](../lifecycle.md#claims-ledger)), both receipts and every comparator log committed at HEAD unmodified, and HEAD contained in `origin/<branch>` (local refs; the dry run never fetches); under `--yes` a failed `gh` query is a failure. `--yes` first runs `git fetch --prune --tags origin` with the refspecs `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*` and `+refs/pull/*/head:refs/remotes/origin/pr/*` (GitHub's pull-request heads are published with the repository), 120 s timeout, so the scan covers every branch, tag and pull-request head the remote holds; the first checklist line is then "fetched origin's branches, tags and pull-request heads: the scan covers them" or the `✗` "git fetch origin failed (...): cannot verify what the public flip would publish", which refuses. It also runs `public-safety NAME` (the whole repository when the package is a subdirectory of it: the line then reads "public-safety (whole repository: the package is a subdirectory): ...") and refuses while blocking hits remain, with the checklist line "public-safety: N hit(s) — fix the tree, or publish a fresh-history tree with `repo export`; see `lean-pkg public-safety NAME`" (" (+W warning(s))" after the count when there are warn hits too); warn-only hits give the `WARN` line "public-safety: 0 blocking hit(s), N warning(s) (FAMILIES) — review with `lean-pkg public-safety NAME`" and do not block; `--skip-public-safety` replaces the scan with a `WARN` line. `--json` gains `public_safety` {skipped, hits, tree_hits, history_hits, block_hits, warn_hits, scope (`package` or `repository`), unscanned, unscanned_blocking}. Evidence that exists on disk but that git ignores (the gate and comparator receipts, the comparator logs, and the `comparator-stages/` files, `stages.json` and stage logs, beside them; judged by `git check-ignore -v`, so a force-added tracked file is never reported) is the `WARN` line "evidence on disk is git-ignored, so `git add` skips it: PATH (RULE), ...; un-ignore it: add `!.lean-receipts/` and `!**/.lean-receipts/**` to .gitignore after the ignoring rule (a `!PATH` line for evidence elsewhere), or `git add -f PATH`", RULE being `SOURCE:LINE:PATTERN` such as `.gitignore:3:*.log`; the `✗` for a required file that is not committed names the rule, "not committed: PATH (git-ignored by RULE)". `--json` gains `ignored_evidence[]` {path, rule} | `--yes` `[--dry-run]` `[--skip-public-safety]` `[--agent A]` |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

Exit 1 is also a negative answer here:

- `publish NAME --dry-run`: not ready to publish

## JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `promote-dry-run` (exit 1): `checklist`, `claims_ledger`, `dry_run`, `ignored_evidence`, `name`, `ok`, `one_way_warning`, `public_safety`, `refused`
- `publish-dry-run` (exit 1): `checklist`, `claims_ledger`, `dry_run`, `head`, `ignored_evidence`, `manuscript_findings`, `name`, `next`, `ok`, `page`, `palomar_check`, `ready`

## Examples

The read-only checklist from verified-private to listed, with the exact next commands; exit 1 while not ready.

```bash
lean-pkg publish my-proof
```

The same, also scanning the tree and the git history for private strings.

```bash
lean-pkg publish my-proof --public-safety
```

The same, with the page line rendered from corroborated GitHub Actions runs (page --check --corroborate).

```bash
lean-pkg publish my-proof --corroborate
```

The same, with the page line rendered from attested GitHub Actions receipts (page --check --attested); after the run has expired from the GitHub API, use this instead of --corroborate.

```bash
lean-pkg publish my-proof --attested
```

The promotion checklist that --yes runs; nothing changes (the pre-1.0 `promote my-proof`).

```bash
lean-pkg publish my-proof --yes --dry-run
```

Make the GitHub repository public after the checklist passes again; this cannot be undone in practice.

```bash
lean-pkg publish my-proof --yes
```
